![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14178392/assets/2fd023af7c229d813344ee366b384a5917b69df0d06fabff6466b9ebcc199bb9.png)

Evaluate the triple integral

$$
{∭}_{R}{({x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2})}^{2}\,\text{d}V
$$

over the region $R$ enclosed inside the sphere ${x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}=4$ for $y\le 0$ and $z\le 0,$ shown above.
question.worked_solution:
We will use the change of variables formula in the form

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,dV={∭}_{Δ}\,f(\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ)\,{\rho }^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\,d\rho \,d\theta \,dϕ.
$$

If $(\rho ,\theta ,ϕ)$ are the spherical coordinates of a point, then its Cartesian coordinates $(x,y,z)$ can be found by using the following formulas:

$$
x=\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,y=\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,z=\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ
$$

Notice that the region $R$ represents one-quarter of the sphere of radius $2$ centered at the origin.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14178392/assets/090f210768ffd4a6be529860b54a2906e265427b7d85bcbb07e3101c801740ba.png)

 

As a result, we obtain that in spherical polar coordinates, our region can be expressed as 

$$
Δ=\{(\rho ,\theta ,ϕ)\,:\,0\le \rho \le 2,\,\pi \le \theta \le 2\pi ,\,\frac{\pi }{2}\le ϕ\le \pi \}.
$$

Next, we substitute the spherical polar coordinates into the function $f(x,y,z)={({x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2})}^{2}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x,y,z) & =f(\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ) \\  & ={({\rho }^{2})}^{2} \\  & ={\rho }^{4}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, using the change of variables formula, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{∭}_{R}{({x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2})}^{2}\,\text{d}V & ={∭}_{Δ}{\rho }^{4}\cdot {\rho }^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\,d\rho \,d\theta \,dϕ \\  & ={\int }_{\pi /2}^{\pi }{\int }_{\pi }^{2\pi }{\int }_{0}^{2}{\rho }^{6}\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\,d\rho \,d\theta \,dϕ \\  & ={\int }_{\pi /2}^{\pi }\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\,dϕ\cdot {\int }_{\pi }^{2\pi }d\theta \cdot {\int }_{0}^{2}{\rho }^{6}\,d\rho  \\  & =[-\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ]_{ϕ=\pi /2}^{ϕ=\pi }\cdot [\theta ]_{\theta =\pi }^{\theta =2\pi }\cdot {[\frac{1}{7}{\rho }^{7}]}_{\rho =0}^{\rho =2} \\  & =-(-1-0)\cdot (2\pi -\pi )\cdot \frac{1}{7}(128-0) \\  & =1\cdot \pi \cdot \frac{128}{7} \\  & =\frac{128\pi }{7}\end{aligned}
$$
